q.q: Which is heavier: a kilo of feathers or a kilo of bricks?
q.fun: A kilo is a kilo. The feathers just have better PR.

q.q: How many months have 28 days?
q.fun: Every month has at least 28 days. February is just the only one that stops there.

q.q: What has keys but can't open locks?
q.fun: A keyboard also counts, but it's too busy autocorrecting you.

q.q: If you have only one match and enter a dark room with a candle, a lamp and a fireplace, what do you light first?
q.fun: The match. Always the match. Then panic about which one is next.

q.q: What goes up but never comes down?
q.fun: Your age only goes up. Your phone battery only goes down. Balance.

q.q: Which word is spelled wrong in every dictionary?
q.fun: "Wrong" is always spelled W-R-O-N-G. Correctly wrong.

q.q: What has a neck but no head?
q.fun: A shirt also has a neck and no head, unless someone is wearing it.

q.q: What can you catch but not throw?
q.fun: You can catch a bus too, but please don't throw it.

q.q: What gets wetter the more it dries?
q.fun: A towel: working hard so you don't have to.

q.q: How many sides does a circle have?
q.fun: Mathematicians disagree. Party guests always say two.

q.q: What is always in front of you but can't be seen?
q.fun: Your nose is also always in front of you. You just choose to ignore it.

q.q: What runs but never walks?
q.fun: A nose can run too. Please bring tissues to the party.

q.q: Which is the longest word: "smiles", "elephant" or "rhinoceros"?
opts: Smiles (there's a mile between the s's)
q.fun: Smiles: S, then a mile, then S. Also the best word at any party.

q.q: What has hands but can't clap?
q.fun: A clock has hands and a face, but it can't clap. It just ticks you off.

q.q: What belongs to you but other people use more than you?
q.fun: Your name. And, if you have siblings, your charger.

q.q: What do children get in red envelopes at Lunar New Year?
q.fun: Red envelopes are the only envelopes kids never want to throw away.

q.q: Which square sticky rice cake is a Tết tradition in Vietnam?
q.fun: Bánh chưng is square, the earth; bánh tét is round. Geography you can eat.

q.q: Which flower is a symbol of Tết in northern Vietnam?
q.fun: In the south it's yellow apricot blossom. Same Tết, different team colours.

q.q: What colour is believed to bring good luck at Lunar New Year?
q.fun: Wear red for luck. Wear black if you want to look like a ninja at the family party.

q.q: What do people say to wish someone a happy new year in Vietnamese?
q.fun: Practise it now. Your aunt will ask you to say it in front of everyone.

q.q: What is "first-footing" (xông đất)?
opts: Being the first visitor of the new year
q.fun: The first visitor brings luck for the year. No pressure.

q.q: How many animals are in the Chinese and Vietnamese zodiac?
q.fun: Vietnam has the cat where China has the rabbit. The cat sends its regards.

q.q: Before Tết, families traditionally…
q.fun: Cleaning the house before Tết sweeps out the bad luck. Cleaning on the first day sweeps out the good luck. Timing matters.

q.q: What fruit tree with small orange fruits do people buy for Tết?
q.fun: A kumquat tree full of fruit means a year full of luck. And a living room full of leaves.

q.q: What is a "five-fruit tray" (mâm ngũ quả) used for?
q.fun: Every region has its own five fruits. Every family thinks theirs is the correct one.

q.q: Lunar New Year usually falls between…
q.fun: The lunar calendar follows the moon, so Tết moves every year. The moon refuses fixed dates.

q.q: What do people often play during Tết for fun?
q.fun: Bầu cua cá cọp: the only game where a crab can beat a tiger.

q.q: "Tết Nguyên Đán" is the festival of…
opts: The first morning of the year
q.fun: Nguyên Đán means the first morning. The first lie-in of the year comes right after.

q.q: Which dragon-like performance is common at Lunar New Year?
q.fun: The lion dance scares away bad luck. Loud drums help. So does the confetti.

q.q: What do you say when someone gives you lucky money?
opts: Thank you, and wish them good health
q.fun: Never open a red envelope in front of the giver. Count it later, like a professional.

q.q: On what date is Christmas Day?
q.fun: What does Santa do in his garden? He hoes, hoes, hoes.

q.q: What pulls Santa Claus's sleigh?
q.fun: Why does Santa use reindeer? Because the horses refused to work the night shift.

q.q: What is the name of the red-nosed reindeer?
q.fun: What do you call a reindeer with no eyes? No idea. (No-eye deer.)

q.q: Where does Santa traditionally live?
q.fun: The South Pole is where penguins live. Santa checked: no reindeer parking there.

q.q: What do people hang by the fireplace for gifts?
q.fun: Why do we hang stockings? Because socks were too small for the gifts we wanted.

q.q: What do you call a person made of snow?
q.fun: What do snowmen eat for breakfast? Frosted flakes.

q.q: Which plant do people kiss under at Christmas?
q.fun: Kissing under a cactus is also possible, but much less popular.

q.q: What is a "carol"?
q.fun: Why was the Christmas tree bad at singing carols? It kept getting the needles wrong.

q.q: "Feliz Navidad" means "Merry Christmas" in which language?
q.fun: Merry Christmas in French is "Joyeux Noël". Noël is just Christmas with a French accent.

q.q: What do you call the small helpers who make toys for Santa?
q.fun: Elves are great at maths: they always know who is naughty and who is nice.

q.q: What is "Boxing Day" (UK)?
q.fun: No boxing on Boxing Day. Just leftovers and opening more boxes.

q.q: What does "sleigh" mean?
q.fun: Sleigh and slay sound the same. Santa's sleigh definitely slays.

q.q: Gingerbread is flavoured with…
q.fun: Why did the gingerbread man go to the doctor? He was feeling crumby.

q.q: What do people put on top of a Christmas tree?
q.fun: The star sits at the top because it's the tree's best idea.

q.q: What is the opposite of "naughty" on Santa's list?
q.fun: Santa's list is the world's oldest database with only two columns.

q.q: What is a carved pumpkin with a candle inside called?
q.fun: Why did the pumpkin win the race? It had a good head start.

q.q: What do children usually say at the door on Halloween?
q.fun: What do ghosts say at the door? Boo or treat!

q.q: On what date is Halloween?
q.fun: Halloween falls on 31 October. Easy to remember: Oct 31 = Dec 25 in programmer maths. Ask a coder.

q.q: In which country did Halloween traditions mostly begin?
q.fun: The old Celtic festival of Samhain started it. The Irish brought it to America, the Americans brought the candy.

q.q: Which animal is a classic witch's pet?
q.fun: Why don't black cats go to parties? They never get a clean bill of health.

q.q: What does a vampire drink in stories?
q.fun: Why are vampires bad at art? They can only draw blood.

q.q: What is a "skeleton"?
opts: All the bones of a body
q.fun: Why didn't the skeleton go to the party? He had no body to go with.

q.q: Which word means "full of ghosts"?
q.fun: Haunted vs hunted: one has ghosts, the other has hunters. Both are bad for a quiet night.

q.q: What does a witch traditionally fly on?
q.fun: Why do witches fly on brooms? Vacuum cleaners have cables that are too short.

q.q: What colour pairs are most typical for Halloween?
q.fun: Red and green? That's Christmas trying to arrive early, as usual.

q.q: What do you call a costume party guest dressed as a monster made by Dr Frankenstein?
q.fun: Fun fact: Frankenstein is the doctor, not the monster. The monster never even got a name.

q.q: A mummy is wrapped in…
q.fun: Why don't mummies take holidays? They're afraid they'll relax and unwind.

q.q: Which creature turns into a wolf when the moon is full?
q.fun: Werewolves love calendars: they always know when it's a full moon.

q.q: What is "candy" called in British English?
q.fun: Americans say candy, Brits say sweets, kids say MORE.

q.q: What does "spooky" mean?
q.fun: Spooky is scary with a smile. Like your phone at 1% battery.

q.q: How many continents are there (by the most common count)?
q.fun: Why did the continents drift apart? They needed some space. About 200 million years of it.

q.q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
q.fun: The Pacific is so big it never says goodbye. It just waves.

q.q: How many hours are there in a week?
q.fun: 168 hours a week and you still "had no time" for homework. Interesting.

q.q: What colour do you get when you mix blue and yellow?
q.fun: Blue plus yellow makes green. Monday plus no coffee makes a monster.

q.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
q.fun: Why is the hexagon so calm? It has every side covered.

q.q: Which language has the most native speakers?
q.fun: English has the most learners. That is why it keeps saying sorry.

q.q: What is the capital of Australia?
q.fun: Sydney wanted the job, Melbourne wanted the job, so they built Canberra. Classic office politics.

q.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
q.fun: A leap year gives you one free day. Most people spend it asleep.

q.q: What is the smallest prime number?
q.fun: Two is the only even prime. It is odd being that even.

q.q: Which instrument usually has 88 keys?
q.fun: 88 keys and it still cannot open a single door.

q.q: How many minutes are there in two and a half hours?
q.fun: 150 minutes: the length of one "quick" meeting.

q.q: Which shape has three sides?
q.fun: Why did the triangle never win arguments? It always ended up in a corner. Three, actually.

q.q: Which gas do plants take in from the air?
q.fun: Plants take in CO₂ and give back oxygen. Your roommate takes your snacks and gives back nothing.

q.q: What is H₂O?
q.fun: Add one more O and you get hydrogen peroxide. Do not drink the one with the extra O.

q.q: At sea level, water boils at…
q.fun: A watched pot never boils. An ignored pot boils over. Pots are dramatic.

q.q: What is the hardest natural material?
q.fun: Diamond is the hardest natural material. Second place: getting up on Monday.

q.q: Which force keeps us on the ground?
q.fun: I am reading a book about anti-gravity. I cannot put it down.

q.q: What is the centre of an atom called?
q.fun: Never trust an atom. They make up everything.

q.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
q.fun: Mercury is liquid at room temperature. So is my motivation: it just runs away.

q.q: Roughly how fast does light travel?
q.fun: Light is faster than sound. That is why some people look bright until they speak.

q.q: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
q.fun: A herbivore walks into a salad bar. Everyone shouts: finally, a regular!

q.q: Which part of a plant makes food from sunlight?
q.fun: Leaves cook with sunlight. Imagine skipping lunch because it is cloudy.

q.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
q.fun: Au is gold and Ag is silver. Chemists clearly lost the naming meeting.

q.q: Which gas makes up most of the air we breathe?
q.fun: Air: 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 1% the smell of someone’s lunch.

q.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
q.fun: Mercury is closest to the Sun. Its sunscreen bill is astronomical.

q.q: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
q.fun: Mars is red because everyone keeps sending robots to stare at it.

q.q: What is the largest planet in our Solar System?
q.fun: All the other planets could fit inside Jupiter. It still says it is big-boned.

q.q: Which planet is famous for its bright rings?
q.fun: Saturn has many rings and has never been married. Respect.

q.q: What is the name of our galaxy?
q.fun: How do you organise a party in space? You planet.

q.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
q.fun: I tried the restaurant on the Moon. Great food, no atmosphere.

q.q: Who was the first human in space?
q.fun: Gagarin reached space in 1961. Most of us still have not left the bed today.

q.q: What does a light-year measure?
q.fun: A light-year is a distance, not a time. So no, your diet did not take light-years.

q.q: How long does Earth take to go around the Sun?
q.fun: Every birthday you finish another lap around the Sun. Still no medal.

q.q: What is the closest star to Earth?
q.fun: The closest star is the Sun. It still shows up late every winter morning.

q.q: What do we call a space rock that lands on Earth’s surface?
q.fun: A meteorite is a space rock that forgot to check the weather.

q.q: Which planet spins on its side?
q.fun: Uranus spins lying on its side. Honestly, same after lunch.

q.q: What is the largest animal ever known?
q.fun: A blue whale’s heart is as big as a small car. Its love life is still complicated.

q.q: A group of lions is called a…
q.fun: Lions move in a pride. Cats move only when you are trying to sleep.

q.q: What is the fastest land animal?
q.fun: Never play cards with a big cat. Everyone knows they are cheetahs.

q.q: How many legs does a spider have?
q.fun: Eight legs. Imagine the sock budget.

q.q: Which mammal can truly fly?
q.fun: Flying squirrels do not fly. They are just very confident gliders.

q.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
q.fun: Why do kangaroo mums hate rainy days? The kids play inside.

q.q: What do giant pandas mostly eat?
q.fun: Pandas spend about half the day eating. Finally, an animal with my priorities.

q.q: Which animal is famous for changing its colour?
q.fun: I looked for the chameleon all day. It was next to me the whole time.

q.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
q.fun: Three hearts and still nobody texts back.

q.q: Which bird is a symbol of wisdom in many cultures?
q.fun: Owls look wise because they rarely talk. Try it in your next meeting.

q.q: Which of these animals can sleep standing up?
q.fun: Horses sleep standing up. So do I, on the morning bus.

q.q: What kind of animal is a dolphin?
q.fun: Dolphins are smart, social and always smiling. The extroverts of the sea.

q.q: What is the main ingredient of guacamole?
q.fun: Avocado is a fruit, so guacamole is basically a smoothie with chips.

q.q: Pizza Margherita comes from which country?
q.fun: Pizza is round, comes in a square box and is eaten as triangles. Explain that.

q.q: Sushi is a traditional dish from…
q.fun: Sushi chefs never panic. They are always on a roll.

q.q: What is tofu made from?
q.fun: Tofu has no taste of its own, so it copies its friends. Very social food.

q.q: Phở is a famous dish from…
q.fun: Want an argument? Ask whether phở is better in Hà Nội or Sài Gòn. Then run.

q.q: Which spice is so pricey it is called “red gold”?
q.fun: Cooking with saffron is basically wearing jewellery in the kitchen.

q.q: What do bees make?
q.fun: What did the bee say after work? Sweet, job done.

q.q: In the saying, which fruit a day keeps the doctor away?
q.fun: An apple a day keeps the doctor away. An onion a day keeps everyone away.

q.q: Which drink is made from roasted beans?
q.fun: Decaf coffee is like a hug from a stranger: nice, but why?

q.q: What is the main ingredient of hummus?
q.fun: Chickpeas are neither chicks nor peas. Food names lie to us.

q.q: Which country is most famous for croissants?
q.fun: A croissant is bread that went to fashion school.

q.q: What is a bánh mì?
q.fun: Bánh mì is a sandwich that went on a gap year and came back cooler.

q.q: Which river is traditionally listed as the longest in the world?
q.fun: The Nile and the Amazon still argue about who is longer. Rivers have egos.

q.q: What is the highest mountain above sea level?
q.fun: Everest: the highest mountain with the lowest Wi-Fi.

q.q: Which is the largest country by area?
q.fun: Russia has 11 time zones. Someone there is always just waking up.

q.q: What is the largest hot desert?
q.fun: Why do deserts never throw parties? Too dry. Nobody comes.

q.q: Which country has had the most people since 2023?
q.fun: India passed China in 2023. The queue jokes write themselves.

q.q: What is the capital of Japan?
q.fun: Kyoto was the capital for about a thousand years. Tokyo took the job without an interview.

q.q: What is the capital of Canada?
q.fun: Everyone guesses Toronto. Ottawa is used to it.

q.q: Which country is shaped like a boot?
q.fun: Italy is a boot kicking Sicily. Rude, honestly.

q.q: The Equator crosses which of these continents?
q.fun: The Equator is an imaginary line. Still more real than my weekend plans.

q.q: What is the smallest country in the world?
q.fun: You can walk across Vatican City before your coffee gets cold.

q.q: Mount Fuji is in which country?
q.fun: A Japanese saying: climb Fuji once and you are wise; climb it twice and you are a fool.

q.q: Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?
q.fun: The Indian Ocean is the warmest ocean. Great for holidays, terrible for ice cream.

q.q: What were the rulers of ancient Egypt called?
q.fun: Pharaohs built pyramids. We cannot even build a flat-pack shelf.

q.q: In which year did World War II end?
q.fun: History teachers love dates. Shame they never bring snacks.

q.q: Who was the first President of the United States?
q.fun: Legend says Washington could not tell a lie. He would fail every job interview today.

q.q: In which year did the Titanic sink?
q.fun: They called it unsinkable. Never say that in a group chat.

q.q: Which empire built the Colosseum?
q.fun: Rome was not built in a day. Neither is my homework.

q.q: Who built the first European printing press with movable type (about 1440)?
q.fun: Gutenberg invented printing. Printers have been “out of paper” ever since.

q.q: Which ancient wonder is still standing today?
q.fun: Built to last 4,500 years. Unlike phone chargers.

q.q: In which year did Vietnam declare independence?
q.fun: Every 2 September the whole country gets a holiday. Best history lesson ever.

q.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
q.fun: The wall fell in 1989. Bricklayers everywhere took it personally.

q.q: Which civilisation built Machu Picchu?
q.fun: Machu Picchu sits about 2,400 m up. The Inca really did not want surprise visitors.

q.q: The Vikings came from which region?
q.fun: Vikings did not really wear horned helmets. Costume designers did.

q.q: The Great Wall was built in which country?
q.fun: You cannot see the Great Wall from space with the naked eye. Your mistakes, however…

q.q: What is the most famous film award in Hollywood?
q.fun: The statue is called Oscar. Nobody knows his surname.

q.q: What do we call the main character of a story?
q.fun: The main character always survives. The one who says “I’ll be right back” never does.

q.q: “Bollywood” is the nickname of the film industry in…
q.fun: Songs, dances, fights and romance in one film. Great value for money.

q.q: “Nollywood” is the film industry of…
q.fun: Nollywood makes a huge number of films each year. Your watch-later list is shaking.

q.q: A film that continues an earlier story is a…
q.fun: A prequel is the first part, made second. Hollywood maths.

q.q: What is a “spoiler”?
opts: Information that gives away the ending
q.fun: Spoiler: this quiz ends after the last question.

q.q: Films made from drawings or models that move are called…
q.fun: Animators draw up to 24 frames for one second of film. Patience level: legendary.

q.q: Mickey Mouse belongs to which studio?
q.fun: Mickey first appeared in 1928 and still has no grey hair.

q.q: A film about real events with real people is a…
q.fun: A documentary about sloths: two hours long, three minutes of action.

q.q: A funny TV series about the same people, episode after episode, is a…
q.fun: Sitcom means situation comedy. My life is just the situation part.

q.q: What does a film director do?
opts: Leads the making of the film
q.fun: Directors shout “Action!”. Parents shout “Bedtime!” with less success.

q.q: Popcorn became a cinema favourite during which decade?
q.fun: Popcorn saved cinemas in the 1930s. It still saves boring films today.

q.q: How many lines are there in a standard music staff?
q.fun: Why could the band not find their composer? He was Haydn.

q.q: Which instrument usually has six strings?
q.fun: Guitarists tune for 20 minutes and play for 5. That is the job.

q.q: Who composed “Für Elise”?
q.fun: Beethoven kept composing after losing his hearing. Some neighbours dream of that.

q.q: How many keys does a standard piano have?
q.fun: Pianoforte means soft-loud in Italian. So the piano’s real name is a volume setting.

q.q: A group of four musicians is a…
q.fun: A quartet: four musicians and one argument about tempo.

q.q: What does the K in K-pop stand for?
q.fun: K-pop dance routines are harder than most gym classes.

q.q: How loud or soft music is played is called…
q.fun: Forte means loud, piano means soft. Musicians whisper in Italian.

q.q: The speed of a piece of music is its…
q.fun: My running tempo: fast for ten seconds, then very slow forever.

q.q: Which instrument is played by blowing and pressing three valves?
q.fun: Trumpet players are experts at blowing their own horn.

q.q: Mozart was born in which present-day country?
q.fun: Mozart composed his first pieces at five. At five I was eating crayons.

q.q: How many performers are in a duet?
q.fun: A duet is two people singing. A duel is two people arguing about who sings.

q.q: Karaoke comes from which country?
q.fun: Karaoke means “empty orchestra”. It fills up fast with brave singing.

q.q: How many players does a football (soccer) team have on the pitch?
q.fun: 22 players chasing one ball. Someone please buy more balls.

q.q: How long is a marathon?
q.fun: Running a marathon: 42 km. Reading about it: 0 km and much nicer.

q.q: Which sport uses a shuttlecock?
q.fun: Badminton is serious business. Ask any Vietnamese park at 6 a.m.

q.q: How often are the Summer Olympics held?
q.fun: Athletes train four years for ten seconds. I cannot commit to a ten-minute workout.

q.q: In tennis, what word means zero?
q.fun: In tennis, nothing is called love. Deep, really.

q.q: In basketball, how many points is a shot from behind the arc?
q.fun: Why are basketball players messy eaters? They always dribble.

q.q: Table tennis was invented in which country?
q.fun: England invented it. China then took it very, very seriously.

q.q: The Tour de France leader wears a jersey of which colour?
q.fun: The leader wears yellow. Everyone else wears sweat.

q.q: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
q.fun: Five Olympic rings and not one of them is gold. Ironic.

q.q: Which martial art comes from Korea?
q.fun: Taekwondo is all about kicks. Handy for doors when your hands are full.

q.q: In golf, one stroke under par on a hole is a…
q.fun: Golf: a long walk with lots of shouting at a tiny ball.

q.q: How many players does a volleyball team have on court?
q.fun: Volleyball players never feel alone. They always have a set.

q.q: What does CPU stand for?
q.fun: The CPU is the brain of the computer. Mine boots after coffee.

q.q: Wi-Fi connects devices…
q.fun: I named my Wi-Fi “Hack it if you can”. Next day it was called “Challenge accepted”.

q.q: Which digits does binary use?
q.fun: There are 10 kinds of people: those who understand binary and those who don’t.

q.q: In computing, one kilobyte is traditionally…
q.fun: 1,024 instead of 1,000. Computer people cannot even round properly.

q.q: What does URL stand for?
q.fun: URL: the thing everyone shouts across the office. “Just send me the link!”

q.q: Which company makes the iPhone?
q.fun: Why did the phone wear glasses? It lost its contacts.

q.q: What is “phishing”?
opts: Tricking people into giving away personal data
q.fun: If an email says you won a prize you never entered, the only prize is a virus.

q.q: What does AI stand for?
q.fun: I asked an AI for a joke about itself. It said it was still processing.

q.q: Which language gives a web page its structure?
q.fun: HTML walks into a bar. The bartender: sorry, we don’t serve your <type>.

q.q: Who designed the Analytical Engine, an early computer, in the 1830s?
q.fun: Babbage designed a computer in the 1830s. It still had no “remind me later” button.

q.q: What does “www” stand for?
q.fun: In English, saying “www” takes longer than saying “World Wide Web”. Efficient.

q.q: A small program you install on a phone is an…
q.fun: There is an app for everything except finishing your homework. Wait…

topics.name: Games
topics.desc: Video games, board games and gamer talk

q.q: In chess, which piece moves only diagonally?
q.fun: The bishop moves diagonally. Like me, avoiding my manager in the corridor.

q.q: Tetris was created in which country?
q.fun: Tetris teaches life: mistakes pile up, successes disappear.

q.q: What does NPC mean in games?
q.fun: NPC life: standing in one spot saying the same line all day. Also called customer service.

q.q: What does “GG” usually mean at the end of a match?
q.fun: GG means good game. “GG EZ” means you need to work on your manners.

q.q: In Minecraft, which green creature explodes near you?
q.fun: Creepers: the only friends who come close just to blow up your house.

q.q: What does Pac-Man eat as he moves through the maze?
q.fun: Pac-Man: a hungry circle chased by ghosts. Same as me at midnight.

q.q: What is Super Mario’s job?
q.fun: Mario is a plumber who never fixes a single pipe. He just jumps into them.

q.q: Which company publishes the main Pokémon games?
q.fun: Pokémon trainers walk thousands of kilometres. Fitness apps hate this one trick.

q.q: In games, what does “respawn” mean?
opts: Come back after being knocked out
q.fun: In games you respawn. In real life you say “five more minutes” and go back to sleep.

q.q: What does “lag” mean in online games?
opts: A delay in the game’s response
q.fun: Lag: when you lose and it is definitely the internet’s fault.

q.q: What is an “Easter egg” in a game?
q.fun: Developers hide Easter eggs in games. My mum hides real ones and I still cannot find them.

q.q: How many squares are on a chessboard?
q.fun: 64 squares and somehow the knight still takes the strangest route.

q.q: What is the capital of Vietnam?
q.fun: Hà Nội: where crossing the street counts as cardio.

q.q: Which river forms the big delta in southern Vietnam?
q.fun: Markets on the Mekong float. Try that with a supermarket.

q.q: Hạ Long Bay is famous for its…
q.fun: Hạ Long has around 1,600 islands. Imagine the property tax.

q.q: What is the traditional Vietnamese long dress called?
q.fun: Áo dài: elegant on stage, heroic on a motorbike.

q.q: What is the highest mountain in Vietnam?
q.fun: Fansipan has a cable car now. Hikers prefer not to talk about it.

q.q: Tết is the celebration of…
q.fun: During Tết, every relative asks when you are getting married. Hide in the kitchen.

q.q: Which old town is famous for its lanterns?
q.fun: Hội An at night: almost more lanterns than tourists. Almost.

q.q: Đà Lạt is known as the city of…
q.fun: People go to Đà Lạt just to wear the jackets they never use.

q.q: What is Vietnam’s currency?
q.fun: Everyone in Vietnam is a millionaire. In đồng.

q.q: Vietnam’s map is often compared to which letter?
q.fun: S-shaped. S for seriously good food.

q.q: Which treat is eaten at the Mid-Autumn Festival?
q.fun: Mooncakes: delicious, and heavy enough to stop a door.

q.q: Water puppetry (múa rối nước) comes from which region?
q.fun: Water puppets: the only actors who never complain about getting wet.

q.q: In emails, what does ASAP mean?
q.fun: In emails, ASAP means “yesterday, please”.

q.q: What does FYI mean?
q.fun: FYI: this joke is for your information only. No reply needed.

q.q: Finish the office joke: “This meeting could have been…”
q.fun: And this email could have been a sticky note.

q.q: What is a “deadline”?
opts: The latest time to finish a task
q.fun: Deadlines are like alarm clocks: one snooze and suddenly it is Friday.

q.q: An “out of office” reply means the person is…
q.fun: Out of office: the three most beautiful words in email.

q.q: What does CC mean in an email?
q.fun: CC: the polite way of saying “my boss can see this”.

q.q: To “touch base” with someone means to…
opts: Contact them briefly to check in
q.fun: Let’s touch base, circle back and align. Translation: let’s talk later.

q.q: When should you use “Reply all”?
opts: Only when everyone needs your answer
q.fun: Reply all: how one “Thanks!” turns into 300 emails.

q.q: What is a CV?
opts: A document about your education and work history
q.fun: Curriculum vitae is Latin for “please hire me”. Roughly.

q.q: “Remote work” means working…
q.fun: Remote work: shirt on top, pyjamas below.

q.q: What is a “colleague”?
q.fun: A colleague: someone who borrows your stapler forever, with a smile.

q.q: To “brainstorm” means to…
q.fun: Brainstorm: ten people, one whiteboard, zero markers that work.

q.q: What do you need to travel to most other countries?
q.fun: My passport photo looks like I was arrested for being tired.

q.q: Why do people get jet lag?
opts: Their body clock and the local time do not match
q.fun: Jet lag: you are in Paris but your stomach is still in Hà Nội asking for phở.

q.q: On a plane, an aisle seat is…
q.fun: Aisle seat: easy toilet trips. Window seat: total control of the sunshine.

q.q: The Eiffel Tower is in…
q.fun: The tower grows a few centimetres in summer heat. So do I after holiday food.

q.q: At a hotel, “check-in” means…
q.fun: Check-in at 2 p.m., check-out at 11 a.m. Hotels invented time travel.

q.q: The Statue of Liberty stands in…
q.fun: The statue was a gift from France. I got a croissant crumb once.

q.q: What is the currency of Japan?
q.fun: Some Japanese coins have holes. Easy to carry, easier to lose.

q.q: A souvenir is…
opts: Something you buy to remember a trip
q.fun: Souvenirs: things you buy abroad and keep in a drawer forever.

q.q: What is a visa?
opts: Official permission to enter a country
q.fun: A visa lets you in. A Visa card lets you shop. Do not mix them up at the border.

q.q: The Great Barrier Reef is off the coast of…
q.fun: The reef is visible from orbit. Fish still get lost.

q.q: Which city is famous for gondolas on canals?
q.fun: Venice has no cars. Its traffic jams are made of boats and selfie sticks.

q.q: A round-trip ticket takes you…
q.fun: Round trip: because you cannot stay on holiday forever. Sadly.

q.q: “Break a leg!” means…
q.fun: Not literally, please. We have no insurance.

q.q: “It’s a piece of cake” means it is…
q.fun: If it is a piece of cake, why am I still hungry?

q.q: “Feeling under the weather” means feeling…
q.fun: Technically, we are all under the weather.

q.q: “Hit the books” means…
q.fun: Not literally. Books have feelings. And sharp corners.

q.q: “Spill the beans” means…
q.fun: Spill the beans, just not on my keyboard.

q.q: If something “costs an arm and a leg”, it is…
q.fun: My phone cost an arm and a leg. Now I can’t even hold it.

q.q: “Once in a blue moon” means…
q.fun: I clean my room once in a blue moon. Mum says the moon must be very blue.

q.q: “Hit the sack” means…
q.fun: The sack did nothing wrong, though.

q.q: “Let the cat out of the bag” means…
q.fun: Why was the cat in the bag in the first place? Asking for a friend.

q.q: “The ball is in your court” means…
q.fun: Please return it. It is my only ball.

q.q: “Let’s call it a day” means…
q.fun: Hi, Day. You were long.

q.q: “Bite the bullet” means…
q.fun: I would rather bite a burger.

q.q: Choose the correct word: “She ___ to work every day.”
q.fun: Third person adds -s. The s is for “she’s so busy”.

q.q: “I have lived here ___ 2019.”
q.fun: Since for a point in time, for for a period. Forever for my student loan.

q.q: What is the plural of “child”?
q.fun: One child: cute. Several children: please bring coffee.

q.q: What is the past tense of “go”?
q.fun: Go becomes went. No logic, just vibes.

q.q: “There are ___ people here.”
q.fun: Many for countable, much for uncountable. Much stress, many deadlines.

q.q: What is the opposite of “always”?
q.fun: Never say never. Oops.

q.q: “___ going to the park after school.”
q.fun: There, their, they’re: three words that sound the same and end friendships.

q.q: What is the comparative of “good”?
q.fun: Good, better, best. Never let it rest… until lunch.

q.q: “If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.”
q.fun: “If I were rich” is correct grammar and my daily dream.

q.q: Which one is a correct question?
q.fun: The last one sounds like a small green movie wizard. Great fighter, bad English teacher.

q.q: Which is correct?
q.fun: An hour, because the h is silent. Like me in morning meetings.

q.q: What is the past participle of “write”?
q.fun: Written is written. It is in writing.

q.q: What has keys but cannot open locks?
q.fun: 88 keys and still locked out.

q.q: What gets wetter the more it dries?
q.fun: A towel’s whole life is a contradiction. Relatable.

q.q: What has hands but cannot clap?
q.fun: Clocks have hands and a face and still never smile at you at 6 a.m.

q.q: What can you catch but not throw?
q.fun: You can catch a cold and a bus. Only one is worth running for.

q.q: What has a neck but no head?
q.fun: A bottle has a neck and no head, so it never gets headaches.

q.q: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
q.fun: Free philosophy, included in this quiz.

q.q: What has one eye but cannot see?
q.fun: A needle has an eye and still cannot find the haystack.

q.q: What goes up but never comes down?
q.fun: Age goes up and never comes down. Neither do prices.

q.q: If you have it, you want to share it. If you share it, you no longer have it.
q.fun: Once you share a secret, it belongs to everyone.

q.q: What has many teeth but cannot bite?
q.fun: A comb has lots of teeth and never needs a dentist.

q.q: Which month has 28 days?
q.fun: Every month has 28 days. February just stops there to rest.

q.q: How many letters are in “the alphabet”?
q.fun: You expected 26. Count the letters in “the alphabet”. Riddles are like that.

q.q: How many bones does an adult human have?
q.fun: Babies have around 300 bones that fuse later. You were more complex as a baby.

q.q: What is the largest organ of the body?
q.fun: Your skin is your biggest organ. Moisturise accordingly.

q.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
q.fun: Four chambers and still no room for Mondays.

q.q: Which blood cells carry oxygen?
q.fun: Red blood cells deliver oxygen all day. Best delivery service, zero tips.

q.q: How many teeth does an adult usually have, including wisdom teeth?
q.fun: Wisdom teeth arrive when you are old enough to regret things.

q.q: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
q.fun: Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day. More when the boss says “quick chat?”

q.q: Where is the smallest bone in the body?
q.fun: The smallest bone is in your ear. Maybe that is why nobody listens.

q.q: About how much blood does an adult have?
q.fun: About 5 litres. Mosquitoes call it a buffet.

q.q: What is the main job of the lungs?
q.fun: Your lungs have worked non-stop since birth with no holiday. Respect.

q.q: Which vitamin does your skin make in sunlight?
q.fun: Vitamin D from the sun. Vitamin Sea from the beach.

q.q: Roughly what share of an adult’s body is water?
q.fun: You are about 60% water. Basically a cucumber with opinions.

q.q: Which sense uses the tongue?
q.fun: Thousands of taste buds and none of them like Mondays.

q.q: What is a budget?
q.fun: A budget: the plan you make on day 1 and forget on day 2.

q.q: Interest on a savings account is…
q.fun: Banks pay interest. I pay attention. Barely.

q.q: “Profit” is…
q.fun: Profit = revenue minus costs minus the snacks you “invested” in.

q.q: Which of these is a cryptocurrency?
q.fun: Bitcoin price: up, down, sideways. Like a cat walking on a keyboard.

q.q: What does CEO stand for?
q.fun: CEO: the person who sends the emails nobody reads to the end.

q.q: “Wholesale” means selling…
q.fun: Wholesale prices: the dream. Retail prices: the reality.

q.q: What is a startup?
q.fun: Startups have bean bags, free snacks and big dreams.

q.q: Which country uses the euro?
q.fun: The UK and Switzerland kept their own money. Very polite “no, thank you”.

q.q: What is an invoice?
opts: A bill that asks for payment
q.fun: An invoice: a polite letter that says “pay me” in a table.

q.q: Inflation means…
q.fun: Inflation: your money stays the same size, your coffee gets smaller.

q.q: A discount is…
q.fun: Discount: buying things you do not need because they are 30% off.

q.q: A receipt is…
q.fun: Receipt and recipe: one shows what you paid, one shows what you will burn.
